discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including giant TMR in MgO-barrier junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently showed large tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions. This turned Julliere's spin-dependent tunnelling, long seen as a low-temperature curiosity, into a robust quantum effect that can be engineered. In 2004 Parkin, and independently Yuasa's group, showed that crystalline MgO barriers filter electrons by the symmetry of their Bloch states, giving magnetoresistance of hundreds of percent. That result confirmed the theoretical predictions and became the basis of a technology. Magnetic tunnel junctions now serve as the read heads in every hard-disk drive and as the storage element of spin-transfer-torque MRAM, which semiconductor foundries now make as non-volatile embedded memory for energy-efficient computing. This work follows the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance and goes further, because it uses quantum tunnelling and spin-polarized band structure to deliver a working technology. A surprising physical effect in a nanostructure became the foundation of global information technology.
